title: Arkret Recovery Completion Carriers
description: Closed recovery completion attestation and Standard-grant issuance carriers. Device recovery is authorized by the accepted PCR recovery policy; an optional DID-root proof is only one explicitly enabled factor. When deployment policy permits reactivation, the same completed closure is the only operation that may atomically author a deactivated-to-active successor for the original account before issuing its new-generation Standard grant.

canonical_public_material.description: Typed public material plus the exact canonical bytes persisted by the coordinator. canonical_bytes_base64url MUST decode to the canonical JSON/CBOR representation of value and digest MUST recompute over those bytes.

issue_recovery_completion_grant_outcome.description: Exact durable outcome for one completed recovery transaction. If the original account was deactivated, successful issuance also means the Account Authority atomically restored that same account and authored its deactivated-to-active successor; no replacement account or second PCR is created.

issue_recovery_completion_grant_request.description: Closed request proving completed PCR recovery and the exact current replacement device generation. The Account Authority checks the committed re-anchor through its RealmCommit.

initial_session.description: The Standard grant to issue after recovery. device_id MUST equal the attested replacement device and the RFC 7638 thumbprint of session_public_key MUST equal the Bound AccountHandoff and HTTP DPoP key.

canonical_request_digest.description: SHA-256 of JCS(request object with only canonical_request_digest omitted). The Bound AccountHandoff authorization and RFC 9449 HTTP DPoP proof authenticate the account and holder outside this closed business body.

recovery_completion_attestation.description: Coordinator-signed proof created after one atomic recovery commit accepted the two producer-signed recovery Events, issued one PCR-stream RealmCommit for each of them, advanced the device generation, activated the replacement device, consumed the recovery session and completed the transaction. A RealmCommit accepts exactly one Event, so the two CommittedEventRef values MUST name two different Commits at consecutive positions n and n+1 of the same PCR Realm stream; their commit_id and their event_id MUST both differ.

account_id.description: Exact recovered account. Its station_id is the coordinator: the service signer/route authority of the Station-local recovery transaction. No separate coordinator field exists on wire or in the signed projection.

completed_at.description: Server-side linearized commit time of the single atomic recovery commit. It MUST NOT be earlier than the terminal receipt completed_at, which is only an authoring time.

signature.description: Base64URL signature over the closed completion projection, including reanchor_event_ref, device_authorization_event_ref and result_model_generation_ref.

reanchor_event_ref.description: CommittedEventRef of the recovery re-anchor Event in the account PCR stream. It sits at position n, immediately before device_authorization_event_ref, in its own RealmCommit.

device_authorization_event_ref.description: CommittedEventRef of the replacement-device authorization Event. It sits at position n+1 of the same PCR Realm stream as reanchor_event_ref, in its own RealmCommit accepted by the same atomic recovery transaction.
